title: Per-run manifest (manifest.json), raw contract 2.8.0
description: One per run, under raw/{source}/_manifests/{extraction_date}/{run_id}/. Strict at the top level and on each captures[] entry: a field not listed here is a contract change. objects, totals, config and finality stay free-form, and so does each endpoint's block except its optional drift (2.4.0, #85), non_2xx_by_gameweek and throughput (2.8.0, #116) blocks, which are strict. captures is present only once the run is finalized; consumers must ignore IN_PROGRESS manifests. 2.5.0 (#54): a response that is not a valid capture is stored under raw/fpl/_invalid/{class}/ and not as payload.json; it has a captures[] entry with usable false and a class, and its endpoint counts as failed. 2.6.0 (#109): a finalized manifest carries invalid_counts, the number of invalid captures per class, and abort_reason when the run stopped itself after consecutive http_error responses. 2.7.0 (#115): an invalid capture the caller declared expected carries expected true (on its sidecar and captures[] entry) and is tallied in its endpoint's expected count instead of failed; the count is absent when zero. 2.8.0 (#116): the entry-picks endpoint (raw/fpl/entry-picks/{season}/{gw}/{entry_id}/...) adds non_2xx_by_gameweek and throughput to its endpoints block, and a run that stopped dispatching at its wall-clock budget carries stop_reason; both are absent otherwise.

invalid_counts.description: Invalid captures in the run per class (#109). Zero-filled; finalized manifests only. fetch_failed stores nothing and is not counted.

abort_reason.description: Why the run stopped itself (#109). Absent when it did not. aborted_http_error_streak: N consecutive http_error responses; in-flight requests finished and the manifest was written.

stop_reason.description: Why the run chose to stop dispatching before it ran out of work (2.8.0, #116). Absent when it did not. stopped_at_budget: the stage's wall-clock budget was spent; in-flight requests finished, unreached entries are absent (not failed), and a rerun resumes. Not a failure by itself: a stop that captured nothing new also marks the endpoint failed, so the run exits non-zero.

captures.description: One entry per body written in the run, valid or invalid. Fetch failures have no body and no entry.

non_2xx_by_gameweek.description: entry-picks only (2.8.0, #116): per gameweek the run requested, how many non-2xx picks responses it stored (not_found and http_error; a 2xx that failed its shape check and a fetch that stored nothing are not counted). Resumed entries are not requests and are not counted. Zero is recorded, so a quiet gameweek reads differently from one not requested. Present only when the run made at least one picks request.

throughput.description: entry-picks only (2.8.0, #116): what the run's picks requests cost, to size the wall-clock budget. requests excludes entries skipped by resume; total_seconds is the stage's wall time; requests_per_second is requests / total_seconds (0 when total_seconds is 0); gameweeks_completed lists the gameweeks whose settlement marker this run wrote. Present only when the run made at least one picks request.

endpoint_drift.description: Payload drift aggregated over the endpoint's captures (#85). Finalized manifests only; warn-only.

origin.description: Where the run came from (#75). kind is ci when GITHUB_ACTIONS is "true", else local; workflow, ref and github_run_id are the Actions run's values for ci and null for local. These are a self-report, not proof. aws_principal is the role or IAM user name STS resolved the run's credentials to, "root" for the root user, null when the lookup failed; never an ARN, account ID or session name. Production is the consumer's call, e.g. kind == ci and ref == refs/heads/main.

key.description: Full object key under the bucket, no scheme.

usable.description: Written, shape_ok and not an invalid response. Always false for an entry with a class.

class.description: Present only on an invalid response, whose key is under raw/fpl/_invalid/{class}/.

expected.description: Present, and true, only on an invalid capture the caller declared legitimate for its request (2.7.0, #115). Absent otherwise, never false.

season.description: From this run's bootstrap-static; null when the run had no usable one.
